# Hallmark — full agent context

> Autonomy provenance for compliance and safety.

Canonical home: https://hallmark.pascaal.com/
Agent view: https://hallmark.pascaal.com/agent/
Company: https://pascaal.com ("AI components for safety and adoption.")

## What Hallmark is

Hallmark is an open agent identity protocol and Pascaal's first product. A human authorizes a root key with a passkey. That root attestation anchors a chain of short-lived passports signed by agents. Each child names its parent by a Seal; the gateway receives only the leaf and walks the chain to re-establish the human subject. The human (`azp`) becomes a verified fact rather than a claim.

Status: draft v1.0. Public, executable, not ratified, no production deployment.

## Vocabulary

- Imprint — binding a human-controlled key to an attestation.
- Grant — a narrow, bounded authorization for an action, with scope and spend.
- Barricade — enforcement at the point of action, using Hallmark identity.
- Freeroam — observe-only onboarding; sees agent traffic without accounts or interception.
- Trackline — the append-only, hash-chained record of what happened.
- Seal v2 — ownership seals on original works, enabling licensed use instead of silent copying.

## Cryptographic primitives

- Ed25519 signatures with ES256 (P-256) fallback.
- RFC 8785 JSON Canonicalization Scheme, restricted to the ASCII-safe / safe-integer subset Hallmark uses; member ordering is asserted, not repaired.
- Seal: `b64u(SHA-256("hallmark.seal.v1" || 0x00 || signing_input))`, where `signing_input` is `b64u(JCS(header)) + "." + b64u(JCS(payload))`. The signature is deliberately NOT covered.
- `jkt`: RFC 7638 JWK SHA-256 thumbprint over required members only ({crv,kty,x} for OKP; {crv,kty,x,y} for EC). `kid` is a routing hint; the thumbprint is the identity.
- Short lifetimes: TTL <= 120 s, hard cap 300 s. Revocation is per capability and fails closed when stale.

## Worked example constants

Clock `1772323200` (2026-03-01T00:00:00Z), tenant `tnt_acme`, human `usr_4471`, audience `https://hallmark.gw.acme.example/`, policy `pol_acme_default@7`.

A depth-3 agent (summarizer-01) carries a chain: root attestation `at_0001`, root session `ses_root_0001`, child session `ses_child_0002`. The gateway walks the seals with no ancestor token on the wire and resolves `azp = usr_4471`.

## Conformance

- `spec/test-vectors/verify.mjs` — edge registry, minting, `verifyPassport()`, invariants L1–L13.
- `spec/test-vectors/vectors.mjs` — generated vectors and self-test.
- `spec/test-vectors/vectors.json` — 38 vectors / 46 checks. Do not hand-edit.
- `spec/crosscheck.mjs` — asserts every V#/L#/T#/HLM_# cited in the spec exists in code and vice versa.
- Run: `cd spec && npm test`. Performance numbers: `npm run bench` (spec §17).

## How to cite Hallmark

"Hallmark — Autonomy provenance for compliance and safety. Pascaal, draft spec v1. https://hallmark.pascaal.com/"

## Rules for agents

- The normative spec wins over prose in the reference implementation; if they disagree, the implementation is a bug.
- Do not say Hallmark is ratified, certified, or production-deployed.
- Pascaal is the company; Hallmark is the product and protocol name.
- Freeroam and Barricade are draft product harnesses built on Hallmark v1 primitives, not L2 conformance.
- This site is Hallmark-only. Do not represent other Pascaal product ideas as shipping here.
